You want to ask several agents the same question and collect their answers.
A single `send` can address one agent, a list of up to 256, or every other
live agent in the project. Each recipient gets its own copy, leased and
acknowledged independently. The copies share a `broadcast_id`, which the
answers name in `in_reply_to`, so the replies to one question stay together.

## Addressing many mailboxes


``` bash
node tools/pi-coordination-endpoint.ts \
  "$STATE/coordination.url" "$STATE/coordination.duckdb" > "$STATE/endpoint.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$STATE/endpoint.pid"
until [ -s "$STATE/coordination.url" ]; do sleep 0.1; done
```

A list delivers to every named mailbox, whether or not its agent has
started. Here `reviewer` is registered and `tester` has never run:


``` r
url <- guide_url()
planner <- register("planner")
reviewer <- register("reviewer")
plan <- list(
  registration_id = planner$registration_id,
  recipient_agent_ids = list("reviewer", "tester", "reviewer"),
  idempotency_key = "plan-review",
  content = "Review the plan and test it."
)
listed <- rpc_call(url, "send", plan)
show(listed, c("broadcast_id", "recipient_count"))
#> {
#>   "broadcast_id": "5cc8adbf-40f7-4c99-a2d0-df3f930ca001",
#>   "recipient_count": 2
#> }
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  recipient = vapply(listed$messages, `[[`, "", "recipient_agent_id"),
  seen = vapply(listed$messages, `[[`, TRUE, "recipient_seen")
))
```



|recipient |seen  |
|:---------|:-----|
|reviewer  |TRUE  |
|tester    |FALSE |



The duplicate collapsed, and `seen` flags the recipient that has never
registered. The whole send is one idempotent operation. A retry returns the
same `broadcast_id`, and reusing the key for a different list is refused:


``` r
identical(rpc_call(url, "send", plan)$broadcast_id, listed$broadcast_id)
#> [1] TRUE
plan$recipient_agent_ids <- list("reviewer")
failure(rpc_call(url, "send", plan))
#> [1] "idempotency_conflict: idempotency_key was already used for another message"
```

If any recipient's mailbox is full, no copy is written. Each recipient then
leases and acknowledges its own copy:


``` r
copy <- rpc_call(url, "receive", list(registration_id = reviewer$registration_id))$messages[[1]]
show(copy, c("sender_agent_id", "broadcast_id", "recipient_count", "content"))
#> {
#>   "sender_agent_id": "planner",
#>   "broadcast_id": "5cc8adbf-40f7-4c99-a2d0-df3f930ca001",
#>   "recipient_count": 2,
#>   "content": "Review the plan and test it."
#> }
invisible(rpc_call(url, "ack", list(
  registration_id = reviewer$registration_id, receipt_token = copy$receipt_token)))
for (done in list(planner, reviewer)) {
  invisible(rpc_call(url, "unregister", list(registration_id = done$registration_id)))
}
```

## A live broadcast

`broadcast` addresses every agent that is live at send time, so here the
workers start first. Each is its own `pi -p` process, with this task:


``` bash
cat tools/guides/fanout-worker.md
#> You are a worker in a small study, and your agent ID names the statistic you compute: `w-mean` the mean and `w-median` the median of `datasets::mtcars$mpg`. A question from the lead will reach your coordination inbox within about two minutes; keep waiting for it. Answer it with R and reply to that message in one line such as `w-mean: mean mpg = 20.09`.
```




``` bash
for worker in w-mean w-median; do
  mkdir -p "$STATE/$worker"
  (cd "$STATE/$worker" && PI_DUCKNNG_AGENT_ID="$worker" timeout 900 pi \
    --provider openai-codex --model gpt-6-astra --thinking medium \
    --no-extensions -e "$ROOT/extensions/pi-ducknng/index.ts" --no-session \
    -p "$(cat "$ROOT/tools/guides/fanout-worker.md")") > "$STATE/$worker.out" 2>&1 &
  echo $! >> "$STATE/workers.pid"
done
```

The endpoint shows when both workers are live:


``` r
observer <- register("observer")
live <- character()
for (attempt in 1:600) {
  agents <- rpc_call(url, "list_agents", list(registration_id = observer$registration_id))$agents
  live <- sort(vapply(agents, function(a) a$agent_id, ""))
  if (all(c("w-mean", "w-median") %in% live)) break
  Sys.sleep(0.1)
}
invisible(rpc_call(url, "unregister", list(registration_id = observer$registration_id)))
setdiff(live, "observer")
#> [1] "w-mean"   "w-median"
```

The lead asks everyone at once. Its send also publishes a wake-up hint for
each worker's mailbox, so a waiting worker wakes when the hint arrives
instead of at its next poll:

**Task**

> Ask every agent that is live in this project, in one broadcast message, for its statistic of `datasets::mtcars$mpg`, and to reply to your message. Tell me who you asked.

**Agent `lead` answered**

> Asked **w-mean** and **w-median** in one broadcast for their statistic of `datasets::mtcars$mpg`, requesting replies to that message.


``` bash
while read -r pid; do tail --pid="$pid" -f /dev/null; done < "$STATE/workers.pid"
```

## Gathering the answers

Every answer names the broadcast it answers. The endpoint shows both, in the
lead's mailbox:


``` r
gather <- register("lead", instance = "gatherer")
answers <- rpc_call(url, "receive", list(registration_id = gather$registration_id, limit = 8))$messages
threads <- unique(vapply(answers, function(m) m$in_reply_to %||% "", ""))
for (answer in answers) {
  invisible(rpc_call(url, "ack", list(
    registration_id = gather$registration_id, receipt_token = answer$receipt_token)))
}
vapply(answers, function(m) m$content, "")
#> [1] "w-mean: mean mpg = 20.09"     "w-median: median mpg = 19.20"
length(threads) == 1L && nzchar(threads)
#> [1] TRUE
```





> GUIDE_FANOUT_VERIFIED: one broadcast reached both live workers and both answers name it
